hot.title: Qwen-AgentWorld: Language World Models for General Agents
hot.summary: Qwen-AgentWorld introduces a family of language world models (LWMs) that simulate diverse agentic environments, surpassing frontier LLMs on the AgentWorldBench and improving agent performance across various downstream tasks. These models enhance agent learning through scalable, controllable simulation and by integrating internal predictive reasoning for action refinement.

hot.title: Tmax: A simple recipe for terminal agents
hot.summary: Researchers at the Allen Institute for AI and the University of Washington developed TMAX-15K, a large and diverse dataset of complex terminal tasks, alongside a simple reinforcement learning (RL) training recipe for open-weight language models. This approach enabled TMAX-9B to achieve 27.2% on Terminal-Bench 2.0, making it the top-performing open-weight model under 10 billion parameters at the time of publication and surpassing several larger models.

hot.title: OpenThoughts-Agent: Data Recipes for Agentic Models
hot.summary: This research systematically investigates and establishes an open data curation pipeline for training broadly capable agentic language models, identifying effective strategies for supervised fine-tuning (SFT) data and demonstrating its efficacy with a new dataset that improves agentic model performance. The study also explores reinforcement learning (RL) data curation, finding that specific RL data sources can induce exploratory agent behaviors and further enhance capabilities when combined with SFT.

hot.title: Unlimited OCR Works
hot.summary: Unlimited OCR introduces a model for one-shot, long-horizon parsing of multi-page documents, employing a Reference Sliding Window Attention (R-SWA) mechanism to maintain a constant KV cache size and stable inference speed. The model achieved an overall score of 93.23% on OmniDocBench v1.5, representing a 6.22 percentage point improvement over its baseline, while efficiently processing continuous document streams.

hot.title: Wan-Streamer v0.1: End-to-end Real-time Interactive Foundation Models
hot.summary: The Wan Team at Alibaba Group developed Wan-Streamer v0.1, an end-to-end streaming foundation model for full-duplex multimodal interaction, integrating language, audio, and video. It demonstrates a model-side response latency of 200 ms and a total interaction latency of 550 ms, supporting real-time, natural human-AI communication with continuous visual presence and dynamic turn-taking.

hot.title: Autodata: An agentic data scientist to create high quality synthetic data
hot.summary: Autodata introduces an agentic framework for autonomously generating and curating high-quality synthetic data to train large language models (LLMs). Through iterative feedback and meta-optimization of the data generation process, it produces data that optimally challenges target models, leading to performance improvements of up to 13.2% in CS research tasks and 17.0% in legal reasoning tasks, while enhancing reasoning efficiency in mathematical problems.

hot.title: Tapered Language Models
hot.summary: This work introduces Tapered Language Models (TLMs), an architectural principle that monotonically decreases a parameter-bearing component's capacity, specifically MLP width, across model depth while maintaining a fixed total parameter budget. The approach consistently improved average commonsense reasoning accuracy and perplexity across diverse architectures and scales, achieving up to 1.84 perplexity points improvement on a 440M Transformer compared to uniform baselines.

hot.title: You Don't Need to Run Every Eval
hot.summary: Microsoft Research developed BENCHPRESS, a system leveraging the observed rank-2 structure of LLM benchmark scores to predict a model's full performance profile from a small subset of evaluations. The system achieves a median absolute error of 4.6 score points on unseen data and can recover model rankings with 92.1% accuracy, significantly reducing evaluation costs.

hot.title: Agent-as-a-Router: Agentic Model Routing for Coding Tasks
hot.summary: The Agent-as-a-Router framework, instantiated as ACRouter, introduces a dynamic, self-adaptive model routing paradigm for coding tasks, continuously learning from execution-grounded feedback to select optimal Large Language Models. This approach achieves the lowest cumulative regret and improved cost-efficiency on a new benchmark, CodeRouterBench, demonstrating strong generalization to out-of-distribution agentic programming tasks.

hot.title: JAXBench: Benchmarking Autonomous TPU Kernel Optimization
hot.summary: JAXBench introduces a TPU-native benchmark suite to evaluate autonomous kernel optimization methods, featuring 50 JAX workloads derived from production LLMs and providing device-side profiling for accurate measurement. The benchmark demonstrates that state-of-the-art LLM agents can achieve a 1.36x geomean speedup over XLA compilation, reaching about 77% of hand-tuned Pallas kernel performance on specific compute-bound tasks.

hot.title: NatureBench: Can Coding Agents Match the Published SOTA of Nature-Family Papers?
hot.summary: This work introduces NatureBench, a benchmark and automated pipeline (NatureGym), to evaluate AI coding agents' ability to surpass published scientific state-of-the-art (SOTA) across 90 tasks derived from Nature-family papers. It finds that current frontier agents achieve limited SOTA surpassing (max 17.8% of tasks) and moderate SOTA matching (max 47.8%), relying primarily on generic ML engineering rather than novel scientific discovery.

hot.title: InSight: Self-Guided Skill Acquisition via Steerable VLAs
hot.summary: INSIGHT introduces a framework for Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models to autonomously acquire new manipulation skills by identifying missing primitive actions and generating their own training data. The system enables robots to continually expand their learned skill vocabulary, achieving high success rates in novel tasks while retaining prior capabilities and improving execution efficiency.

hot.title: World Value Models for Robotic Manipulation
hot.summary: This research introduces the World Value Model (WVM), which repurposes spatiotemporal priors from video world models to achieve a generalist robotic value estimator with enhanced temporal understanding. It establishes a new evaluation benchmark, Suboptimal-Value-Bench, demonstrating WVM's superior ability to track task progress in suboptimal scenarios and guide robust policy learning from mixed-quality data.

hot.title: Are We Ready For An Agent-Native Memory System?
hot.summary: This research systematically evaluates existing large language model agent memory systems from a data management perspective, introducing a four-module analytical framework and conducting extensive empirical studies across 12 architectures and five benchmark workloads. The study provides insights into architectural trade-offs, operational costs, and how different memory components impact task effectiveness, retrieval fidelity, and dynamic update robustness.

hot.title: TuringViT: Making SOTA Vision Transformers Accessible to All
hot.summary: The Foundation Model Team at Xpeng Inc. introduced TuringViT, a Vision Transformer designed for enhanced accessibility of state-of-the-art visual encoders through an efficient linear-attention-dominant architecture, a sophisticated data curation pipeline, and native dynamic-resolution training. This system achieved competitive performance on vision and multimodal benchmarks using substantially less pre-training data and demonstrated improved inference efficiency for high-resolution inputs.

hot.title: Improved Large Language Diffusion Models
hot.summary: Researchers at Renmin University of China and ByteDance developed iLLaDA, an 8-billion parameter fully bidirectional masked diffusion language model, achieving performance competitive with leading autoregressive models and substantial improvements over prior diffusion LLMs across various benchmarks.

hot.title: Self-Compacting Language Model Agents
hot.summary: A training-free framework called SELFCOMPACT enables large language model (LLM) agents to autonomously manage their context by adaptively deciding when and what to summarize using a rubric-based mechanism. This approach improves task performance by up to 18.1 points on math reasoning and 9.2 points on agentic search, while reducing token costs by 33-67%.

hot.title: AsyncOPD: How Stale Can On-Policy Distillation Be?
hot.summary: Researchers introduced AsyncOPD, an asynchronous pipeline for on-policy distillation (OPD) that efficiently trains large language models (LLMs) for reasoning tasks, addressing the challenge of stale data and finite teacher-score caches. This system delivers up to a 3.8x throughput speedup over synchronous methods while maintaining model accuracy.

hot.title: MAS-PromptBench: When Does Prompt Optimization Improve Multi-Agent LLM Systems?
hot.summary: A new benchmark, MAS-PromptBench, systematically quantifies the effects of prompt optimization in multi-agent LLM systems, revealing that while optimization can improve performance by up to 24.0 percentage points in specific setups, it can also cause degradations of up to 16.0 points, with outcomes heavily influenced by task type, communication structure, and team size.

hot.title: Causal-rCM: A Unified Teacher-Forcing and Self-Forcing Open Recipe for Autoregressive Diffusion Distillation in Streaming Video Generation and Interactive World Models
hot.summary: The paper introduces Causal-rCM, a framework for autoregressive video diffusion distillation that unifies teacher-forcing consistency models (TF-CM) with self-forcing distribution matching distillation (SF-DMD). This approach achieved leading VBench-T2V scores in streaming video generation with as few as 1 or 2 sampling steps and was successfully applied to interactive world models.

likes.title: ParallelKernelBench: Can LLMs Write Fast Multi-GPU Kernels?
likes.summary: ParallelKernelBench (PKB), a new benchmark and evaluation framework, assesses the ability of large language models (LLMs) to generate high-performance multi-GPU kernels. The evaluation shows frontier LLMs struggle with complex distributed parallelism, achieving limited correctness and speedup in single-shot settings, though they occasionally produce 'net new' kernels that outperform PyTorch+NCCL baselines for specific workloads.

likes.title: HoloAgent-0: A Unified Embodied Agent Framework with 3D Spatial Memory
likes.summary: HoloAgent-0, a unified embodied agent framework developed by Horizon Robotics and D-Robotics Robotics, bridges the divide between large language model reasoning and real-world physical robot execution. It integrates persistent 3D spatial memory and a structured skill interface to facilitate robust, closed-loop task execution, demonstrating high success rates in real-robot navigation and competitive performance in semantic mapping.

likes.title: Krea 2 Technical Report
SeFi-Image: A Text-to-Image Foundation Model with Semantic-First Diffusion
likes.summary: SeFi-Image is a text-to-image foundation model that leverages a Semantic-First Diffusion paradigm to achieve high-quality image generation. The model produces competitive or superior results on benchmarks for prompt following, text rendering, and bilingual generation, notably with substantially reduced training computational cost compared to other leading models.

likes.title: MeshFlow: Mesh Generation with Equivariant Flow Matching
likes.summary: MeshFlow generates high-quality 3D triangle meshes using an equivariant optimal-transport flow matching model applied to a triangle soup representation. The method achieves an 18.55x speedup over autoregressive baselines, generating meshes in under a second, while improving fidelity and reducing self-intersections to 7.97% on categories like Lamp.

likes.title: Lift4D: Harmonizing Single-View 3D Estimation for 4D Reconstruction In-the-Wild
likes.summary: Carnegie Mellon University researchers developed Lift4D, a test-time optimization framework that reconstructs complete 4D (3D geometry and motion) representations of dynamic, non-rigid objects from monocular in-the-wild videos. The system integrates causal latent propagation for temporal consistency and occlusion-aware appearance refinement with view-conditioned diffusion priors, demonstrating improved perceptual quality, temporal coherence, and semantic fidelity over prior methods on synthetic and real-world datasets.

likes.title: Sakana Fugu Technical Report
likes.summary: Sakana AI's Fugu and Fugu-Ultra are learned orchestrators that combine specialized Large Language Models (LLMs) into a collective intelligence, dynamically generating agentic workflows to leverage their complementary strengths. The system achieved state-of-the-art performance on various benchmarks, scoring 73.7 on SWE Bench Pro, 82.1 on Terminal Bench 2.1, and 95.5 on GPQA-Diamond, often surpassing individual frontier models.

likes.title: SPIRAL: Learning to Search and Aggregate
likes.summary: The SPIRAL framework trains large language models to optimize the combined use of sequential, parallel, and aggregative inference compute end-to-end. This approach yields models that achieve up to 11x higher scaling efficiency in pass@k and 13.5% greater performance with recursive self-aggregation on mathematical reasoning tasks.

likes.title: ReNIO: Reweighting Negative Trajectory Importance for LLM On-Policy Distillation
likes.summary: Researchers introduce ReNIO, a reweighting mechanism for on-policy distillation (OPD) in large language models that emphasizes negative (incorrect) reasoning trajectories. ReNIO consistently improved mathematical reasoning and code generation performance by up to 15.44% relative to baselines, doing so while preserving the efficiency of short-prefix training.

likes.title: CLI-Universe: Towards Verifiable Task Synthesis Engine for Terminal Agents
likes.summary: CLI-Universe introduces a synthesis engine designed to create high-quality, verifiable training tasks for LLM-based terminal agents, addressing the challenge of limited, ambiguous training data. The generated CLI-Universe-6K dataset enables a Qwen3-32B model to achieve a 33.4% pass rate on Terminal-Bench 2.0, outperforming other open-source models of comparable size and several larger open-weight models.
